analysis.investment_thesis: Active Infrastructures is a small civil construction company — a cyclical, lumpy, capital-intensive business that sits well outside my circle of competence in consumer retail and FMCG. Despite a recent equity infusion cleaning up the balance sheet, debt remains material (INR 60 Cr vs INR 116 Cr equity), OCF is volatile, and P/E of 26x on INR 13 Cr profit offers no margin of safety.
key_strengths: Promoter holding healthy at 72.38%, signals skin in the game
Borrowings reduced from INR 109 Cr (2022) to INR 60 Cr (2025); equity raise strengthened balance sheet
Revenue scaled from INR 1 Cr to INR 90 Cr with expanding EBITDA margin (~31% in 2025)
key_risks: Civil construction is cyclical, order-book dependent, working-capital heavy — not a steady compounder
FY25 OCF collapsed to INR 5 Cr vs INR 32 Cr in FY24; FCF only INR 2 Cr — earnings quality questionable
D/E still ~0.52 and ROE of 13.6% is below my 15%+ threshold; P/E 26x is expensive for a contractor
red_flags: Revenue dropped from INR 97 Cr to INR 90 Cr in FY25 — no consistency
Large financing inflow (INR 63 Cr) in FY25 suggests dilution/fundraise to shore up balance sheet
No dividend track record visible; FCF trend is deteriorating (11→5→2 Cr)
analysis.detailed_analysis: This is a INR 267 Cr microcap civil contractor — precisely the kind of business I avoid. Construction is lumpy, working-capital intensive, dependent on government/private order flow, and vulnerable to payment delays. The 348% revenue CAGR is meaningless as it grows off a INR 1 Cr base in 2022; the more relevant read is that revenue went 89→97→90 Cr, i.e., it has plateaued. Net profit of INR 13 Cr on INR 90 Cr revenue (14% net margin) looks optically good for the sector, but FY25 OCF of just INR 5 Cr against reported profit of INR 13 Cr tells me earnings are running ahead of cash — a classic construction-accounting warning.
